2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in short, are that the opposite party No.1 as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No.01 of 2005 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Rainagar, Naogaon for pre-emption of the case land under Section 96 of the Estate Acquisition & Tenancy Act contending inter alia that, the case land of R.S. khatian No.1018 originally belonged to Sudhir Kumer Sarker and Adhirl Kumar Sarker, each of 8 Annas share and case land of R.S. Khatian No.242 belonged to Koshir Uddin Sarder. Kosir Uddin transferred .21 Sotangsho of land in favour of Sree Khitish Chandra vide registered kabala deed No.4405 dated 26.04.1976 and the above mentioned Adhir Kumer Sarker transferred .16 Sotangsho of land in favour of the Kitish Chandra. Thereafter, Kitish Chandra transferred his land in favour of his son Sree Khogendranath vide gift deed No.365 dated 14.01.1998 who transferred "ka" and "kha" schedule land in favour of the pre-emptee petitioner vide kabala deed No.2703 dated 06.06.2004. The pre-emptor is the contiguous land owner and the pre-emptee is the stranger in the case land and the pre-emptee petitioner in collision with opposite party No.2 and without any knowledge of the pre-emptor on 06.06.2004 created the sale deed. The pre-emptor got information about the transfer on 12.12.2004 and on obtaining certified copy on 18.12.2004 finally confirmed about the transfer and filed this case within time. Hence the case. 

 3. The case was contested by the pre-emptee petitioner by filling written objection denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter-alia that, the pre-emptor opposite party No.2 Khogendranath Mohanto obtained the case land on the basis of registered gift deed No.365 of 1998 and for his necessity he wanted to sell the property and verbally approached to the pre-emptor but he refused to purchase the land due to his inability and thereafter, in presence of the pre-emptor as well as the local alite the pre-emptee No.2 transferred the case land to the pre-emptee-petitioner. He further alleged that he is also a co-sharer by purchase of the case land and also a contiguous land holder since he purchased land from the surrounding khatian of the impugned deed. The pre-emption case is to be liable dismissed. 

 10. On the contrary, Mr. Md. Robiul Ahsan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party no.1 argued that both the courts concurrently found that no question of waiver, acquiesces and estoppels, had for defect of parties or limitation in the case. He argued that the appellate court on considering the map of the surrounding khatian decided that the pre-emptor is a contiguous land holder of the case jote which is a right finding. He further argued that the map is a public document and the pre-emptee did not raise any objection about the same, when the same was produced before the appellate court in such a case, at this stage the pre-emptee-petitioner cannot claim that which is not a proper document to consider the case. He prayed for discharge the Rule. 

 11. I have heard the learned Advocates of both the sides, perused the impugned judgment of the courts below, the papers and documents as available on the records. This is a pre-emption case under Section 96 of the Estate Acquisition & Tenancy Act. The pre-emptor claimed that he is a contiguous land holder and without any notice under Section 89 of the Estate Acquisition & Tenancy Act, the pre-emptee No.2 transferred the property to pre-emptee No.1 to deprive the right of the pre-emptor. The trial court after consideration of the evidence on record opined that no question of waiver acquiesces and estoppels in the instant case, not bad for defect of parties and the case filed within time. The appellate court upheld the said findings of the trial court. The trial Court dismissed the case only considering that the pre-emptor failed to prove that he is a contiguous land holder. The appellate Court on considering the concerned 'নকশা' of the Khatians which filed by the pre-emptor at the appellate stage took view that the pre-emptor is a contiguous land holder and thus allowed the pre-emption case setting aside the judgment of the trial court.
